og.description: dadmor's six services in one format: problem, audience, deliverables, scope factors and limits, plus a finder that suggests a service from six questions.

blocks.html: All six services follow one format: the problem they solve, who they are for and who they are not for, what is delivered, and what changes the size of the work. We give a fixed price after a scoping conversation, in a written proposal.

items:
Website building

A website with structure: modeled, built, and handed over with documentation, so it keeps working after launch day.

Not a fit if you only want a ready-made template in your brand colours.

Band S to L by pages, features, integrations and content readiness

About website building

UI/UX design

Interfaces decided by user tasks and evidence, delivered as a system developers can actually build from.

Not a fit if you only need a few screens to show investors.

Band S to L by number of flows and key screens

About UI/UX design

Business model design

A model you can test: assumptions, revenue logic, and kill/continue criteria, not just a convincing pitch deck.

Not a fit if you need a financial forecast or investment advice.

Fixed proposal per phase

About business model design

Documentation

Documents the next maintainer can use, with a named audience, format, and update rule.

Not a fit if the document only needs to exist in a folder.

Fixed proposal per phase

About documentation

Penetration testing

A manual, scoped test with a CVSS-scored report and a retest: proof of what was tested, and what was not.

Not a fit without written authorisation from the system owner, or if you want a "fully secure" certificate.

Fixed-scope proposal after scoping only; one retest included

About penetration testing

Marketing and content

Video, text, and SEO built from the same structure as the product, so content explains the work instead of decorating it.

Not a fit if you want a promised Google ranking.

Monthly band by pieces, channels and SEO work

About marketing and content
